output.risk_summary: Combining Benadryl with alcohol is dangerous and can cause extreme drowsiness, loss of coordination, and slowed breathing that could become life-threatening.

details.finding: Benadryl and alcohol together cause additive central nervous system depression
details.explanation: Diphenhydramine, the active ingredient in Benadryl, makes you drowsy on its own. Alcohol does the same thing. When combined, these effects multiply dangerously — you can become extremely drowsy, lose coordination, have trouble thinking clearly, and in serious cases experience slowed or difficult breathing. This combination significantly increases your risk of accidents, falls, and overdose.
details.source: FDA OTC monograph / clinical literature: diphenhydramine + ethanol

output.what_to_do: Do not drink any alcohol while taking Benadryl, and do not take Benadryl if you have been drinking. Wait at least 12 hours after your last drink before taking Benadryl, or wait at least 6 hours after taking Benadryl before drinking alcohol. If you need allergy relief and plan to drink, consider a non-drowsy antihistamine like loratadine (Claritin) or cetirizine (Zyrtec) instead — but talk to a pharmacist first to make sure these are safe for you. If you've already combined Benadryl and alcohol and feel unusually drowsy, confused, or have trouble breathing, seek medical help immediately.

data.description: Diphenhydramine (found in Benadryl, NyQuil, ZzzQuil, many sleep aids) combined with alcohol causes additive CNS depression: extreme drowsiness, impaired coordination, risk of respiratory depression.
data.management: Avoid alcohol entirely when taking diphenhydramine.
